_readme: The registry for the ajit-segment-bots blueprint. The diagram is drawn from
this file and nothing else. Nothing here is invented: categories and features
come from the user, and each carries the origin it came from.
EVERY PART IS A TRANSISTOR. docs/transistor-rule.md is the shape of a part and
it decides how every feature is built. Six rules, all checked by
dashboard/check_contracts.py and refused by the git pre-commit hook:
T-1  every feature is the same shape -- one template, no exemptions
T-2  control path separate from data path -- only the governor switches parts
T-3  off means genuinely off -- an off part releases its CPU and RAM
T-4  a part knows nothing about the circuit -- it names data, never parts
T-5  states are explicit and countable, drawn from state_vocabulary
T-6  grow by adding parts, never by making a part cleverer
R-01 in docs/contracts.md keeps the data plane whole: edges are computed from
consumes/produces, so a part swaps out cleanly and none can wire itself in.
categories[]       the foundation blocks. Every feature belongs to exactly one.
id, name, summary, origin ('user' | 'proposed'), approved
state_vocabulary[] the closed set of states a part may be in. Extending it is a
deliberate decision, never a smuggled flag (T-5).
data_types[]       id, name, description -- what actually moves between parts
features[]         id, name, role, category, consumes[], produces[], switchable,
off_releases_resources, states[], replaces?
features[] is empty until the user describes them. data_types[] is empty
until the flow between categories is declared. Neither is guessed.

categories.name: Paper trading on live data
categories.summary: Trading runs on live market data, with a switch between real money and paper money.

categories.name: Universal opportunity scanner
categories.summary: Constantly monitors every symbol in the segment and picks when one should enter trading. It holds no built-in rules: what counts as an opportunity arrives as instructions from the hypothesis feature. An opportunity can be anything -- a sudden price jump implying a minor pullback, for instance -- and the response depends on the segment. Lives inside the segment bot. Does not know whether the money is paper or live.

categories.name: Segment bot (bull, bear, profit tailgating)
categories.summary: The container. Inside it: the universal opportunity scanner, the AI brain, and three complete bots — bull, bear and profit tailgating — each its own block (RL-048). The bots issue opinions; the brain turns three opinions into one intent. The scanner raises every candidate to every bot and never learns what they prefer (RL-046).

categories.name: Intelligence
categories.summary: The one global thinker. Sees all three segments at once where every other thinking block sees only its own: total exposure, decision quality as distinct from outcome, the regime itself breaking, and ideas nobody has tried -- including ones it went looking for on the open web. It advises; every trade decision still belongs to a segment.

categories.name: Learning loop
categories.summary: Keeps the score the bots learn from: each bot's right and wrong calls, which features actually preceded profit, and whether a bot has earned its way out of exploration.

categories.name: Hypothesis
categories.summary: Takes what closed trades taught and turns it into opportunity instructions for the scanner. Explicitly includes thinking about how the information in a losing trade becomes an opening profit trade. Further internals not yet described.

categories.name: Knowledge
categories.summary: Three memory tiers that disagree with each other on purpose: semantic facts per symbol upserted under closed-set keys, episodic closed trades appended immutably and keyed on the condition observed, and a procedural playbook that is never searched and always injected. Shape proposed from research, not given by the user.

categories.name: Prediction
categories.summary: Predicts what the market does next, from candles alone. Built on Kronos, the open-source foundation model for K-line sequences: a tokenizer quantises OHLCV into hierarchical discrete tokens, an autoregressive transformer continues the sequence. Both halves are finetuned on the assets actually traded here.

categories.name: Online research
categories.summary: Decodes the portfolios of famous or high-profit crypto traders to copy their strategy or step up beyond it. Reads through front doors only -- venue leaderboard APIs and public chain explorers -- because the data that matters is published, and typed data survives a redesign where scraped HTML does not.

categories.name: LLM services
categories.summary: Infrastructure first: it makes model calls and returns answers, holds no opinion about trading and decides nothing, so there is one place to swap models, cap cost and cache. A reasoning role of its own is a planned extension, not a gap.
categories.planned_extension: Becomes a thinker in its own right once the rest is running — reasoning about the market rather than only answering other blocks' questions.

categories.name: Hardware resource governor
categories.summary: An AI agent that scans the hardware and keeps every other part working without queueing: allocating CPU and RAM, swapping parts fast, turning off a part that is hogging the machine and turning on the part that needs it. This is why R-02 exists -- it cannot turn off a part that has no off switch.

categories.name: Market data feed
categories.summary: Exchange connectivity, reconnects, gap detection and symbol normalisation across venues. The substrate the scanner, prediction and paper-fill pricing all read from.

categories.name: Risk and capital allocation
categories.summary: Position size, leverage, exposure caps, drawdown limits and the kill switch. The bots decide direction; this decides how much, and when to refuse.

categories.name: Ledger and audit trail
categories.summary: Every scan, decision, order, fill and price recorded. What the learning loop learns from, and what hypothesis and prediction are scored against.

categories.name: Portfolio and position state
categories.summary: What is held right now, per segment, reconciled against the exchange. The scanner needs to know what is already open before calling a new entry.

categories.name: Observability
categories.summary: Health and state of every part, feeding the dashboard. As a category it forces each part to emit its own state rather than have it inferred later.

categories.name: Execution and venue adapter
categories.summary: Placing orders for real: partial fills, rejects, retries, rate limits. The user chose it standing on its own rather than nested inside paper/live trading.

categories.name: AI brain
categories.summary: Arbitrates. Each of the three bots emits a direction with conviction; the brain weighs them and issues the single trade intent that leaves the segment bot. This is why it sits inside the segment bot rather than beside it.

categories.name: Closed trade decoding
categories.summary: Decodes finished trades — winners and losers both — into instructions for the hypothesis feature. Portfolio state signals that a position closed; the ledger supplies that trade's full history, every scan, intent, sizing and fill that led to it. The loser is not discarded: its information is what hypothesis works on.

categories.name: Skills
categories.summary: Reads books, research papers, community chats and anything else, and converts each into a skill the brains load on demand. Distilled into structure -- frameworks, decision rules, anti-patterns -- never a summary. Only the section a question needs is loaded, so the library can be large without costing anything until it is used.

categories.name: Autonomous operation
categories.summary: Runs itself with nobody watching, builds its own new parts when it finds a gap, decides inside a named boundary without asking, heals its own breakage. Global: one instance for the whole bot. It never switches a part itself -- it states a need as data and the resource governor acts, which is the only way autonomy and T-2 can both be true.
categories.open: The user gave four jobs and said more is coming: 'andmore i will explann next'. This block is deliberately unfinished, not complete.

categories.name: Backtesting
categories.summary: Replays recorded history against an opportunity instruction, so an idea is tested before the scanner is ever told to watch for it. C-01 forward-tests on live data, which proves an instruction in real time at real cost; this proves it in past time at no cost. Nothing reaches the scanner until it has survived a replay that was audited for look-ahead and charged real costs.

categories.name: Bull bot
categories.summary: A complete bot with its own features, model, scorecard and board cells, issuing the long-side opinion on every candidate the scanner raises. Same skeleton as the other side (T-1), separate at runtime (RL-048).

categories.name: Bear bot
categories.summary: A complete bot with its own features, model, scorecard and board cells, issuing the short-side opinion on every candidate the scanner raises. Same skeleton as the other side (T-1), separate at runtime (RL-048).

categories.name: Profit tailgating bot
categories.summary: A complete bot that joins what is already working: continuation setups from the scanner, this segment's own winning leg of an exploration pair (RL-047), and tracked traders' positions. Never proposes a reversal; always trails, never targets.

categories.name: Capital desk
categories.summary: The user's money settings, read from one file per scope on the server (RL-055) and shown on the board: the main paper balance and its currency, and for every segment bot the balance allocated to it, the largest and smallest capital one trade may use, and the leverage ceiling (RL-051). The desk checks that the allocations add up, converts between currencies at the live rate, journals every change, and proposes — never applies — a rebalance.

categories.name: LLM foundation
categories.summary: The layer every LLM-using part calls through. Prompts are versioned and rendered with retrieved context; every answer is checked against its output schema before any part reads it; prompt versions are scored on golden cases and promoted or refused; each part has a token budget and each decision a cost; memory is embedded and retrieved before reasoning (RL-056). llm-services stays the plumbing that places the call.

categories.name: Broker adapter (Indian markets)
categories.summary: Reads, and later trades through, India's retail broker APIs -- one BrokerAdapter contract that any of the six brokers named in docs/goal.md can satisfy. Upstox is the first and only implementation; part ids are broker-agnostic on purpose, same as execution-venue-adapter never naming Binance or Bybit -- which broker answers is a settings choice, not a part's identity.

categories.name: Stock market news data
categories.summary: Everything the Indian market says about itself, divided by segment. One global block: each source is read once, each item is tagged with the segments it belongs to (index options, stock options, index futures, stock futures, cash equity, commodities), each segment bot filters its own tag. Three channels that never share a wire -- hard facts the executor refuses on (ban, halt, corporate action, session), scheduled events, plus a learned news signal.

data_types.name: market data
data_types.description: One trade, as a venue printed it, normalised across venues. Trades only: candles are `candle` and the book is `order-book-snapshot`, split out on 2026-08-25 after one wire carrying three shapes crashed a reader of one of them.

data_types.name: entry candidate
data_types.description: A symbol, the moment it should enter trading, which watch condition fired and its reading. Never a side. Carries nothing about paper or live.

data_types.name: trade intent
data_types.description: A direction and conviction for a candidate, from the bull, bear and profit-tailgating bots.

data_types.name: sized order
data_types.description: A trade intent with size, leverage and stops applied — or a refusal, which is also an answer.

data_types.name: order request
data_types.description: An order addressed to a destination, after the paper/live switch has chosen one.

data_types.name: fill
data_types.description: What actually executed, at what price, including partials and rejects.

data_types.name: position
data_types.description: What is held right now, per segment, reconciled against the venue.

data_types.name: journal entry
data_types.description: An immutable record of something that happened, with the time it happened.

data_types.name: research finding
data_types.description: A decoded strategy or portfolio from a public high-profit trader.

data_types.name: part health
data_types.description: A part's own state and health, emitted by the part rather than inferred about it.

data_types.name: opportunity instruction
data_types.description: What the scanner should watch for and what it implies. The user's words: opportunities are instructions or feeds derived from the hypothesis feature, not rules built into the scanner.

data_types.name: closed trade
data_types.description: A finished trade with its outcome, profit or loss, and everything that led to it.

data_types.name: decoded trade instruction
data_types.description: What a closed trade taught, drawn from winners and losers alike, expressed as an instruction for the hypothesis feature to work on.

data_types.name: LLM request
data_types.description: A question a block asks a language model. The asking block names this data type, never the LLM block.

data_types.name: LLM response
data_types.description: The model's answer, returned to whichever block asked.

data_types.name: K-line window
data_types.description: A fixed-length run of OHLCV candles, the shape the Kronos tokenizer expects. Bounded by the model's context limit.

data_types.name: price forecast
data_types.description: Predicted candles for the periods ahead, with the model version that produced them.

data_types.name: forecast accuracy
data_types.description: How a past forecast actually scored against what the market did. A forecast nobody scores is an assertion.

data_types.name: finetuned model
data_types.description: Kronos weights adapted to the assets actually traded here, tokenizer included.

data_types.name: model choice
data_types.description: Which Kronos size to run: mini, small or base.

data_types.name: volatility feature set
data_types.description: The ten realised- and implied-volatility features from the reel, computed for one symbol.

data_types.name: volatility forecast
data_types.description: Forward realised volatility estimated from the feature set. Distinct from a price forecast: it says how much, not which way.

data_types.name: implied volatility surface
data_types.description: ATM implied vol, the 30-60 term slope and the 25-delta put skew. Only exists where an options venue does.

data_types.name: market regime
data_types.description: Trending, mean-reverting, or mixed, from a Hurst proxy. Mixed is a real answer meaning stand down.

data_types.name: trade episode
data_types.description: A closed trade keyed on the market condition that was observed, never on the outcome. Immutable.

data_types.name: recalled episode
data_types.description: Past episodes matching a condition seen now.

data_types.name: semantic fact
data_types.description: A durable fact about one symbol, filed under a closed-set key so a contradiction overwrites by construction.

data_types.name: playbook rule
data_types.description: An always-injected, never-searched, capped rule. Behaviour only, never diagnosis.

data_types.name: expectancy breakdown
data_types.description: Expected value split into separately measurable factors, so the weakest one is visible rather than the total merely being poor.

data_types.name: ablation scorecard
data_types.description: What measurably broke when each part was switched off, one row per part.

data_types.name: source document
data_types.description: A source pulled into text, whatever form it arrived in: book, paper, chat log, page.

data_types.name: skill
data_types.description: A source distilled into structure -- frameworks, decision rules, anti-patterns -- with the trigger that says when it applies. Never a summary.

data_types.name: available skill
data_types.description: An indexed skill, findable by what it is for rather than by its title.

data_types.name: loaded skill section
data_types.description: Only the part of a skill the current question needs. This is what lets the library grow without a token cost.

data_types.name: skill usefulness
data_types.description: Whether loading a skill changed the outcome. A skill nobody scores is an assertion.

data_types.name: tracked trader
data_types.description: A high-performing trader worth following, with the venue or wallet that identifies them.

data_types.name: external position
data_types.description: What a tracked trader currently holds, from public explorers or venue leaderboards.

data_types.name: strategy gap
data_types.description: What a decoded strategy does that this bot does not. The 'step up beyond it' half of C-09.

data_types.name: directional opinion
data_types.description: One bot's direction plus conviction on a candidate. An opinion, never an order.

data_types.name: bot scorecard
data_types.description: A bot's own record of right calls against wrong ones. What it learns from.

data_types.name: bot maturity
data_types.description: Whether a bot has graduated out of exploration on its own measured edge.

data_types.name: feature reliability
data_types.description: Which features preceded profitable trades rather than losing ones.

data_types.name: stop adjustment
data_types.description: A protective stop moved up as a position gains, so a pullback keeps some profit rather than giving it all back.

data_types.name: exposure view
data_types.description: Total capital at risk across every segment at once. No per-segment block can compute this; that is the point of it.

data_types.name: decision quality score
data_types.description: Whether the reasoning was sound, scored separately from whether the trade won. A win on luck and a loss on a correct call are different events.

data_types.name: regime break alert
data_types.description: The market has changed enough that what was learned no longer applies.

data_types.name: web idea
data_types.description: Something found by looking rather than by being pointed at it.

data_types.name: novel idea
data_types.description: A strategy nobody here has tried, proposed rather than derived from what already happened.

data_types.name: subscription LLM request
data_types.description: An llm-request routed to the Claude subscription session, because subscription allowance remains.

data_types.name: paid LLM request
data_types.description: An llm-request routed to a metered cloud model API key, because the subscription allowance is spent.

data_types.name: LLM call record
data_types.description: What one answered call actually cost: model, tokens, latency, which route answered it.

data_types.name: LLM quota state
data_types.description: How much subscription allowance is left before the next reset.

data_types.name: LLM spend state
data_types.description: How much money the metered route has spent against its ceiling.

data_types.name: LLM model choice
data_types.description: Which language model answers a given class of request. Distinct from model-choice, which sizes a Kronos forecaster.

data_types.name: restart request
data_types.description: A statement that something has stopped that should be running. It asks; only the resource governor acts on it.

data_types.name: outage state
data_types.description: Whether a venue is reachable right now, how long it has been unreachable, what is stale because of it.

data_types.name: capability gap
data_types.description: Something the circuit cannot yet do, named precisely enough that a part could be written to fill it.

data_types.name: proposed part
data_types.description: A new part the bot wrote for itself: role, consumes, produces, states. Not yet in the circuit.

data_types.name: admitted part
data_types.description: A proposed part that passed every contract check. Only this may enter the circuit, which is what keeps self-authoring from becoming self-corrupting.

data_types.name: autonomy envelope
data_types.description: Which decisions the bot may take without a human, and at what size. The boundary is data in one place, never an assumption spread across parts.

data_types.name: trading halt
data_types.description: A decision that the whole bot stops trading. Risk allocation owns the kill switch; this is what asks it to be pulled.

data_types.name: part fault
data_types.description: A part has stopped behaving: dead, stalled, or reporting health that its output contradicts.

data_types.name: replacement plan
data_types.description: Which admitted part takes over from a faulted one. A plan, not an act -- the governor performs the swap.

data_types.name: survival tier
data_types.description: How much runway is left, graded: full, conserving, critical. A graded scarcity reading, not a part state -- states stay off/on per T-5.

data_types.name: conservation plan
data_types.description: What the bot sheds at a given level of scarcity: which work stops, which model steps down, how much the poll slows.

data_types.name: policy decision
data_types.description: The ruling on one act the bot proposed to take by itself: allow, hold, or refuse, with the rule that decided it and the reason.

data_types.name: modification record
data_types.description: One change the bot made to itself: what changed, the diff, whether it can be undone. Append-only.

data_types.name: upstream change
data_types.description: A newer version of the bot's own code that exists but is not running here yet.

data_types.name: folded circuit map
data_types.description: The whole circuit compressed to a readable size: groups folded to one box each, opened only where a question needs the detail.

data_types.name: order flow state
data_types.description: One second of trade flow labelled as one of fifteen states: the sign of the price change crossed with the volume quintile.

data_types.name: flow entropy
data_types.description: How structured the recent order flow is, on a normalised scale. Low means informed traders are leaving a footprint. Carries no direction, by mathematical necessity.

data_types.name: cointegrated pair
data_types.description: Two symbols whose spread A - beta*B has tested stationary, carrying the hedge ratio, the reversion speed and the measured half-life.

data_types.name: historical window
data_types.description: A bounded run of recorded market history for one symbol, at the resolution a replay needs.

data_types.name: walk-forward split
data_types.description: Training and test windows that never overlap, in time order, with every threshold frozen after training.

data_types.name: cost estimate
data_types.description: What a simulated fill would really have cost: spread crossed, slippage, fees, at that moment on that venue.

data_types.name: backtest run
data_types.description: One replay of one instruction over one split: every simulated entry, exit and fill it produced.

data_types.name: backtest verdict
data_types.description: Whether a replay can be trusted at all -- look-ahead, overlapping windows, survivorship, or a clean bill.

data_types.name: backtest result
data_types.description: What a replay actually earned after costs, per fold, with the concentration of the profit across days.

data_types.name: proven instruction
data_types.description: An opportunity instruction that survived replay. The only kind the scanner is given.

data_types.name: money mode
data_types.description: Paper or live, per segment, set by the user. The only place the money question is answered; the scanner never sees it.

data_types.name: capital allotment
data_types.description: How much paper capital the user has assigned to this segment out of the total portfolio. Editable by the user, journalled on change (RL-040).

data_types.name: account balance
data_types.description: Free plus used balance for the segment right now, paper or live, in the quote currency.

data_types.name: watch condition
data_types.description: A proven instruction compiled into a condition the sweeper can test against every symbol on every tick.

data_types.name: symbol universe
data_types.description: Every symbol the segment can trade right now, as listed by the venue, refreshed as listings change.

data_types.name: liquidity grade
data_types.description: How tradeable a symbol is at the size the bot trades: spread, depth, turnover.

data_types.name: instrument choice
data_types.description: The segment's own answer to a trade intent: which contract, strike, expiry or pair actually expresses it.

data_types.name: cross-segment lesson
data_types.description: A lesson decoded in one segment, restated so another segment can read it. Reported, never enforced.

data_types.name: correlation cluster
data_types.description: Symbols that move together, across segments, so two positions that look different can be seen as one bet.

data_types.name: market event
data_types.description: A scheduled or breaking event that moves markets: token unlock, listing, macro print, exchange notice.

data_types.name: market anomaly
data_types.description: A print, gap or feed that does not look like a market: flash move, stale tick, outlier.

data_types.name: instruction scorecard
data_types.description: What each opportunity instruction has actually earned since it went live, per segment.

data_types.name: forecast trust
data_types.description: How much weight a forecast has earned from its measured accuracy on trades, not on candles.

data_types.name: slippage profile
data_types.description: Measured difference between intended price against filled price, by symbol, size, hour.

data_types.name: inverted hypothesis
data_types.description: A losing trade's information turned around: what the opposite entry would have needed to be true.

data_types.name: hypothesis priority
data_types.description: Which hypotheses are worth writing into instructions first, ranked by measured expectancy.

data_types.name: retired instruction
data_types.description: An instruction withdrawn because it stopped earning or its regime broke. Kept, never deleted.

data_types.name: symbol profile
data_types.description: What is normal for one symbol: typical range, spread, volume by hour, how it reacts to its own jumps.

data_types.name: instruction history
data_types.description: Every instruction ever issued, retired or live, with what it was derived from.

data_types.name: stale knowledge
data_types.description: A fact, skill or instruction that measurably stopped helping, named so it can be pruned rather than rot.

data_types.name: funding forecast
data_types.description: Where the funding rate is headed next period, so a short that pays funding is priced before it is opened.

data_types.name: liquidation map
data_types.description: Price levels where leveraged positions would be liquidated, from open interest, so a stop is not placed where the crowd's is.

data_types.name: ensemble forecast
data_types.description: Price plus volatility forecasts combined by their earned trust into one view ahead.

data_types.name: model drift alert
data_types.description: A forecast model's accuracy has decayed past its floor; retrain it or stand it down.

data_types.name: copy score
data_types.description: How worth copying a tracked trader's current position is, given their verified record plus this segment's own history.

data_types.name: whale transfer
data_types.description: A large on-chain transfer into or out of an exchange, which often precedes a move.

data_types.name: sentiment reading
data_types.description: How the crowd is talking about a symbol right now, graded, with the source counted.

data_types.name: local LLM request
data_types.description: An llm-request routed to a model running on this machine, because no subscription or paid route is usable.

data_types.name: LLM backpressure
data_types.description: How hard to throttle asking: when quota or spend runs low, low-value questions wait.

data_types.name: hardware capacity
data_types.description: What the machine has, what is free right now: CPU, RAM, disk, measured.

data_types.name: part resource usage
data_types.description: What each running part actually costs in CPU plus RAM, measured at runtime, not declared.

data_types.name: hog report
data_types.description: A part using far more than its share while another waits.

data_types.name: part priority
data_types.description: Which parts matter most when there is not enough machine for all of them. The user's order.

data_types.name: switch plan
data_types.description: Which parts to turn on or off next, with the reason, before any gate is touched.

data_types.name: switch record
data_types.description: One gate flipped: which part, on or off, when, by which plan. The control plane's own journal.

data_types.name: order book snapshot
data_types.description: Bids plus asks to depth at one moment, for one symbol.

data_types.name: feed gap
data_types.description: A missing or stale run in market data: which symbol, how long, whether it is still open.

data_types.name: leverage choice
data_types.description: The leverage for one trade, chosen per trade from volatility plus funding, never a fixed setting (RL-041).

data_types.name: stop-target plan
data_types.description: Where the initial stop plus take-profit sit for one trade, before it is sized.

data_types.name: risk limit
data_types.description: The most the segment may risk right now, from every brake at once; the sizer takes the smallest.

data_types.name: USDT PnL statement
data_types.description: Profit or loss in USDT for one trade against the capital it used, converted at the live rate recorded per fill (RL-028, RL-029).

data_types.name: peak excursion
data_types.description: The best plus worst unrealised points a position reached while open (RL-042).

data_types.name: venue position report
data_types.description: What the venue says is held, fetched rather than computed, to reconcile against.

data_types.name: journal gap
data_types.description: A break in the journal: missing sequence, broken hash, or a recorder that stopped.

data_types.name: heartbeat table
data_types.description: Every part's latest health in one table, with how old each entry is.

data_types.name: board snapshot
data_types.description: One rendering of the whole system's measured state, timestamped, every tile traceable to a probe (RL-012).

data_types.name: alert
data_types.description: Something a human should look at now, with the proof attached.

data_types.name: probe result
data_types.description: The output of one measurement that ran, with the command that ran it.

data_types.name: order reject reason
data_types.description: Why the venue refused an order, classified: balance, rate limit, price band, size step, outage.

data_types.name: venue rate budget
data_types.description: How many requests the venue still allows this window.

data_types.name: decision rationale
data_types.description: Why the brain chose this intent, in words, written before the outcome is known.

data_types.name: reflection note
data_types.description: What the brain concluded on rereading its own rationale against what happened.

data_types.name: forecast bias
data_types.description: How far to lean the arbiter toward a forecast this time, given its trust.

data_types.name: loss cause
data_types.description: Why a trade lost, classified: entry, exit, size, regime, execution.

data_types.name: winner pattern
data_types.description: A condition that recurs across winning trades, stated so an instruction can test it.

data_types.name: exit quality
data_types.description: How much of the peak a trade kept when it closed.

data_types.name: skill conflict
data_types.description: Two skills that give opposite advice for the same question.

data_types.name: skill refresh request
data_types.description: A skill that should be re-distilled because its usefulness fell or its source moved.

data_types.name: human override
data_types.description: The user's direct instruction: halt, resume, or cap, which outranks everything the bot decides (RL-038).

data_types.name: live-vs-replay gap
data_types.description: How far paper results drift from what the backtest promised for the same instruction.

data_types.name: board link
data_types.description: The public URL the board was pushed to, with the snapshot time it carries.

data_types.name: fill price estimate
data_types.description: The weighted-average price an order of this size would fill at, from walking live book depth, with whether it cleared fully.

data_types.name: delayed order request
data_types.description: An order request released only after a simulated venue round-trip, so a paper fill can never be faster than a real one.

data_types.name: liquidation price
data_types.description: The price at which this bot's own leveraged position is force-closed by the venue, from entry, leverage and maintenance margin.

data_types.name: locked allocation
data_types.description: Capital earmarked against one sent order, owned but unavailable to a second order until the first fills or is cancelled.

data_types.name: price increment
data_types.description: The smallest price step the venue accepts for a symbol, declared or inferred from live bid/ask spacing.

data_types.name: raw venue order status
data_types.description: One venue's native order status payload, before translation into the system's closed status set.

data_types.name: stamped order
data_types.description: A sized order carrying a client-generated idempotency id, so a resubmit reuses it and the venue deduplicates.

data_types.name: cancel decision
data_types.description: A still-open order that should be pulled: past its time-to-live, or the market has drifted too far from it.

data_types.name: order reprice
data_types.description: A bounded step of an unfilled limit order's price toward the market, on a fixed cadence.

data_types.name: cost basis
data_types.description: The average price a position was actually built at, updated on every fill, zeroed when flat.

data_types.name: funding settlement
data_types.description: One perpetual funding payment, settled as an idempotent event keyed on its settlement boundary.

data_types.name: drawdown episode
data_types.description: One drawdown from peak through recovery or still open: depth, how long it has lasted, how long recovery took.

data_types.name: fill sequence
data_types.description: The order in which pending orders would have filled inside one simulated bar, with the bar split so later checks see the narrowed range.

data_types.name: fillable size
data_types.description: The most a simulated fill may take from one bar, from a participation cap against real traded volume.

data_types.name: feed jump
data_types.description: A candle whose open does not match the prior close: present but discontinuous data, so a stop in the gap still counts as crossed.

data_types.name: forecast out-of-distribution flag
data_types.description: A forecast made from a feature vector far from anything the model was trained on, so it should be discounted regardless of past accuracy.

data_types.name: turbulence index
data_types.description: One market-wide number: how far today's cross-symbol return vector sits from its trailing covariance — is everything moving together abnormally.

data_types.name: verified snapshot
data_types.description: A deterministic, non-LLM rendering of the latest bars, a fixed indicator set and recent closes, that an LLM-backed part is told to defer to.

data_types.name: execution schedule
data_types.description: A sized order split into timed slices, front-loaded when forecast volatility is high, each slice capped by participation.

data_types.name: follow candidate
data_types.description: Something already working that the tailgater may join: a continuation setup, our own winning leg, or a tracked trader's position.

data_types.name: move remaining
data_types.description: How much of a move is likely left against how much has already gone.

data_types.name: crowding reading
data_types.description: How crowded the move already is: funding stretch, book one-sidedness, sentiment extreme.

data_types.name: refutation verdict
data_types.description: Whether a claimed edge survived the refutation battery: placebo treatment, random common cause, data-subset, bootstrap. One failure is a hard disqualifier.

data_types.name: trial ledger
data_types.description: Every hypothesis, retune or parameter trial ever run on a family, counted, so a reported edge can be deflated by how many tries produced it.

data_types.name: forgetting report
data_types.description: How a current model scores on frozen past episodes it once got right, so learning something new is caught overwriting something old.

data_types.name: coverage report
data_types.description: Realised abstention coverage against the coverage the conformal gate promised, per bot, per window.

data_types.name: counterfactual outcome
data_types.description: What the opinion the arbiter did not take would have earned, replayed against the same prices.

data_types.name: cross-segment signal
data_types.description: A reading from one segment restated for another: a spot whale inflow for the futures sweeper, a basis stretch for the spot bots.

data_types.name: competence map
data_types.description: What the system currently knows it is good at, per setup class, regime plus segment, with how sure it is, from its own measured record.

data_types.name: edge half-life
data_types.description: How fast each instruction's measured edge is decaying, stated as a half-life in trades plus in hours.

data_types.name: training label
data_types.description: The outcome a closed trade teaches: which barrier hit first, within what horizon, at what return net of cost.

data_types.name: sample weight
data_types.description: How much one labelled episode should count in training, lower where its holding window overlaps others.

data_types.name: retrain request
data_types.description: A learned part should refit now, with the reason: drift, forgetting, schedule, or enough new labels.

data_types.name: model version
data_types.description: One trained model with its data window, feature list, gate verdicts plus trial count, addressable by id.

data_types.name: champion choice
data_types.description: Which model version a learned part should serve, chosen by the gate, never by recency.

data_types.name: learning reward
data_types.description: What a trade earned restated as the reward a learner optimises: net of cost, risk-adjusted, horizon-discounted.

data_types.name: feature attribution
data_types.description: How much each feature moved each decision, per model version.

data_types.name: bot regret
data_types.description: Cumulative regret of the arbiter's choices against the best single bot in hindsight, per regime.

data_types.name: candidate formula
data_types.description: A machine-found expression over features that predicted an outcome in sample, awaiting falsification.

data_types.name: novelty score
data_types.description: How different a hypothesis is from every instruction ever issued, so a rediscovery is not retested as new.

data_types.name: falsification criterion
data_types.description: Written before the test: the result that would refute this hypothesis.

data_types.name: required sample size
data_types.description: How many trades an instruction needs before its edge is distinguishable from zero at the stated confidence.

data_types.name: mutated hypothesis
data_types.description: A near-miss instruction with one threshold, time-frame or filter varied.

data_types.name: hypothesis regime tag
data_types.description: The regime a hypothesis was born in, carried with it so it can be retired when that regime ends.

data_types.name: knowledge link
data_types.description: An edge between two knowledge items that share a symbol, regime, setup or source.

data_types.name: fact provenance
data_types.description: Where a fact came from, when, with what confidence, plus how fast that confidence decays.

data_types.name: knowledge contradiction
data_types.description: Two knowledge items that cannot both hold.

data_types.name: episode embedding
data_types.description: A vector for an episode's observed condition, never its outcome, for similarity recall.

data_types.name: regime memory
data_types.description: What worked plus what failed in each regime, summarised from episodes.

data_types.name: knowledge snapshot
data_types.description: A hashed snapshot of the whole knowledge state at one moment, so a past decision can be replayed against what was known then.

data_types.name: fact confidence
data_types.description: A fact's current confidence after decay along its forgetting curve, restored when re-confirmed.

data_types.name: verified record
data_types.description: A tracked trader's claimed record checked against what chain or venue data actually shows.

data_types.name: copy latency
data_types.description: How stale an external position is by the time this system sees it, measured.

data_types.name: on-chain flow
data_types.description: Stablecoin mints plus burns, exchange reserve changes, bridge flows: aggregate money moving toward or away from trading.

data_types.name: options flow
data_types.description: Large option block trades: strike, expiry, side, size.

data_types.name: I/O pressure
data_types.description: How saturated disk plus network are right now, separate from CPU plus RAM.

data_types.name: accelerator slot
data_types.description: A GPU or other accelerator allocation granted to one part for one window, if the machine has one.

data_types.name: memory forecast
data_types.description: Minutes until memory runs out at the current growth rate, per part.

data_types.name: restart budget
data_types.description: How many restarts a part has left in its window before it is held off as crash-looping.

data_types.name: duty cycle
data_types.description: The hours each heavy part is allowed to run, so retraining lands in quiet hours.

data_types.name: flap report
data_types.description: A part that has been switched on plus off repeatedly in a short window.

data_types.name: resource reservation
data_types.description: A guaranteed floor of CPU plus RAM for a part that must never be starved: the risk gate, the halt path.

data_types.name: skill backtest
data_types.description: How a distilled skill's rules would have scored on past episodes, before it is indexed.

data_types.name: skill version
data_types.description: One distillation of a skill with its diff from the previous one.

data_types.name: skill gap
data_types.description: A question a brain asked for which no skill was found.

data_types.name: skill provenance
data_types.description: Source, date, licence plus distiller version of a skill.

data_types.name: conflict ruling
data_types.description: What to do when bull plus bear both hold high conviction on one symbol: straddle, pick, or abstain, per regime plus maturity.

data_types.name: bot weight
data_types.description: How much the arbiter trusts each bot right now, sampled from its regret record.

data_types.name: size hint
data_types.description: A conviction restated as a capped fraction of capital, for the sizer to cut further, never raise.

data_types.name: premortem note
data_types.description: Written before the intent leaves: how this trade most plausibly fails.

data_types.name: counter-argument
data_types.description: The strongest case against an intent, written by a part whose job is to disagree.

data_types.name: timed intent
data_types.description: A trade intent released at the moment its entry timing named, or dropped at the give-up time.

data_types.name: venue standing
data_types.description: Whether a venue is currently safe to ask: rate headroom, recent 418/429s, withheld streams, measured latency.

data_types.name: key standing
data_types.description: Whether one API key on one venue is currently safe to use for private calls.

data_types.name: consolidated price
data_types.description: One price per symbol from every venue that quotes it, with each venue's weight plus staleness.

data_types.name: stream plan
data_types.description: Which streams go on which connection to which venue, within measured per-connection plus per-IP limits.

data_types.name: feed coverage
data_types.description: Per symbol, which venues currently supply which data, and where nothing does.

data_types.name: P&L attribution
data_types.description: One closed trade's result split into what direction, timing, size, fees, slippage plus funding each contributed.

data_types.name: entry quality
data_types.description: How close the entry was to the best price available in the window after the signal, in basis points plus bars.

data_types.name: exit counterfactual
data_types.description: What the same trade would have earned under each other exit rail: earlier, later, trailing, time-stop.

data_types.name: horizon profile
data_types.description: How return net of cost evolves with holding time for a setup class, so the best horizon is measured, not chosen.

data_types.name: trade cluster
data_types.description: Closed trades that were effectively one bet: opened together on symbols that moved together.

data_types.name: outcome significance
data_types.description: Whether a trade's result is distinguishable from noise given the symbol's volatility over the hold.

data_types.name: near-miss episode
data_types.description: A candidate that was raised but not traded, with what the market then did, so abstentions teach too.

data_types.name: regime transition flag
data_types.description: Whether the regime changed between a trade's entry plus its exit.

data_types.name: shortfall breakdown
data_types.description: Implementation shortfall split into delay, spread, impact plus opportunity cost.

data_types.name: trade narrative
data_types.description: The trade told in plain words from its journal: why entered, what happened, why exited.

data_types.name: sequence pattern
data_types.description: A pattern across consecutive trades: losses after losses, time-of-day clusters, size creep after wins.

data_types.name: stop audit
data_types.description: Whether a stop was hit by noise before price reached the target: too tight, too wide, or right.

data_types.name: excursion profile
data_types.description: The distribution of best plus worst unrealised points per setup class, from every closed trade.

data_types.name: pair verdict
data_types.description: For an exploration pair on one symbol: which side was right, by how much, and what distinguished the setup.

data_types.name: replay mismatch
data_types.description: A closed trade whose replay from its own journal does not reproduce the ledger's P&L.

data_types.name: Bull bot side candidate
data_types.description: Bull bot's own. An entry candidate one side's bot has kept, with the setup weight it carried.

data_types.name: Bear bot side candidate
data_types.description: Bear bot's own. An entry candidate one side's bot has kept, with the setup weight it carried.

data_types.name: Bull bot feature vector
data_types.description: Bull bot's own. One bot's own features for one candidate: the numbers its model reads.

data_types.name: Bear bot feature vector
data_types.description: Bear bot's own. One bot's own features for one candidate: the numbers its model reads.

data_types.name: Bull bot raw conviction
data_types.description: Bull bot's own. A learned model's probability that the move goes the bot's way by more than cost within the horizon, before calibration.

data_types.name: Bear bot raw conviction
data_types.description: Bear bot's own. A learned model's probability that the move goes the bot's way by more than cost within the horizon, before calibration.

data_types.name: Bull bot calibrated conviction
data_types.description: Bull bot's own. A conviction mapped onto the bot's own measured hit-rate, so 0.7 means 70% for this bot.

data_types.name: Bear bot calibrated conviction
data_types.description: Bear bot's own. A conviction mapped onto the bot's own measured hit-rate, so 0.7 means 70% for this bot.

data_types.name: Tailgater calibrated conviction
data_types.description: Tailgater's own. A conviction mapped onto the bot's own measured hit-rate, so 0.7 means 70% for this bot.

data_types.name: Bull bot entry timing
data_types.description: Bull bot's own. Now, or wait for the pullback the playbook says comes, with a give-up time.

data_types.name: Bear bot entry timing
data_types.description: Bear bot's own. Now, or wait for the pullback the playbook says comes, with a give-up time.

data_types.name: Bull bot exit plan
data_types.description: Bull bot's own. A bot's proposed target, stop and time-stop for its own candidate. Proposed; the risk gate decides.

data_types.name: Bear bot exit plan
data_types.description: Bear bot's own. A bot's proposed target, stop and time-stop for its own candidate. Proposed; the risk gate decides.

data_types.name: Tailgater exit plan
data_types.description: Tailgater's own. A bot's proposed target, stop and time-stop for its own candidate. Proposed; the risk gate decides.

data_types.name: Bull bot setup weight
data_types.description: Bull bot's own. How much one bot trusts each setup class on each time-frame, learned from its own scorecard, applied inside the bot. The scanner never sees it (RL-046).

data_types.name: Bear bot setup weight
data_types.description: Bear bot's own. How much one bot trusts each setup class on each time-frame, learned from its own scorecard, applied inside the bot. The scanner never sees it (RL-046).

data_types.name: Tailgater setup weight
data_types.description: Tailgater's own. How much one bot trusts each setup class on each time-frame, learned from its own scorecard, applied inside the bot. The scanner never sees it (RL-046).

data_types.name: Bull bot feature out-of-distribution flag
data_types.description: Bull bot's outlier rejector found the feature vector far from anything its model has seen; its conviction model abstains. Distinct from the prediction block's forecast-level flag.

data_types.name: Bear bot feature out-of-distribution flag
data_types.description: Bear bot's outlier rejector found the feature vector far from anything its model has seen; its conviction model abstains. Distinct from the prediction block's forecast-level flag.

data_types.name: main account setting
data_types.description: The main paper account as the user set it: total balance and its currency. Edited in the server settings file, never by a part.

data_types.name: trade capital bounds
data_types.description: The largest and smallest capital one trade in this segment may use, as the user set them.

data_types.name: leverage ceiling
data_types.description: The highest leverage this segment bot may choose; the bot picks per trade at or under it (RL-053).

data_types.name: paper currency rate
data_types.description: Live rate from the main account's currency into a segment's quote currency, journalled per conversion (RL-029).

data_types.name: allocation headroom
data_types.description: Main balance minus the sum of segment allocations. Negative means the user has allocated money that does not exist.

data_types.name: capital settings verdict
data_types.description: Whether the capital settings are consistent: min <= max <= allocation, allocation sum <= main balance, ceiling within the chosen instrument's limit. Failing settings zero the risk limit.

data_types.name: bounded order
data_types.description: A sized order after the capital bounds: bumped up to the minimum (RL-054), capped at the maximum. The only order shape execution ever sees.

data_types.name: capital utilisation
data_types.description: How much of a segment's allocation is in positions, locked against orders, or free, right now.

data_types.name: allocation proposal
data_types.description: A proposed move of allocation between segments with its reason and evidence. Shown on the board; the user edits the file or does not.

data_types.name: prompt template
data_types.description: A drafted prompt with its output schema and the part it serves. Drafted, not yet a version.

data_types.name: prompt version
data_types.description: An immutable, numbered prompt plus output schema that the registry currently serves for one part.

data_types.name: prompt promotion
data_types.description: The gate's decision to promote a prompt template to the serving version, or to refuse it, with the scores.

data_types.name: prompt context
data_types.description: Retrieved passages plus the verified market snapshot, assembled for one request.

data_types.name: rendered LLM request
data_types.description: An llm-request with its prompt version and context filled in: what actually goes to the model.

data_types.name: validated LLM output
data_types.description: A model answer that passed its output schema. The only LLM output any part reads.

data_types.name: golden case
data_types.description: A past request with the answer that turned out right, from a closed trade's outcome.

data_types.name: prompt score
data_types.description: How one prompt version scored across the golden cases: accuracy, schema failures, tokens, latency.

data_types.name: LLM part budget
data_types.description: Tokens one part may spend in the window, from its record and the system's allowance.

data_types.name: decision cost
data_types.description: What one trade intent cost in LLM tokens and money, set against what the trade made.

data_types.name: embedding
data_types.description: A vector for one passage of knowledge, journal or decoded trade, with its source.

data_types.name: retrieval query
data_types.description: What to look up for one request, derived from the request.

data_types.name: retrieval hit
data_types.description: Passages ranked for one query, each with its source and score.

data_types.name: retrieval score
data_types.description: How useful retrieved passages proved, measured against the prompt score they fed.

data_types.name: symbol price frame
data_types.description: Every symbol's latest price on one venue, each with the moment it printed, published on a fixed cadence rather than per trade.

data_types.name: market quote
data_types.description: One symbol's best bid and ask on one venue, with the size at each and the moment the venue stamped it. A quote exists whether or not the symbol traded, which is what separates it from a print.

data_types.name: symbol quote frame
data_types.description: Every symbol's latest best bid and ask on one venue, each with the moment the venue stamped it, published on a fixed cadence rather than per quote.

data_types.name: candle
data_types.description: One OHLCV bar for one symbol at one interval, with the venue's own flag for whether the bar is closed. Split from market-data on 2026-08-25: that type carried trades, candles and books at once, and the minute candles began flowing on it feed-gap-detector -- which reads a trade's sequence number -- crashed every two seconds. A candle is a summary of many trades and shares no field with one.

data_types.name: venue premium
data_types.description: One symbol's mark price and index price on one venue, with the funding rate the venue has declared for the next settlement and the moment it settles. The premium is mark minus index as a fraction of the index, and it is what a funding rate is averaged from -- so it is a different fact from the rate itself, which the venue states about a settlement that has not happened yet.

data_types.name: strategy review
data_types.description: A per-bot narrative judgment from an LLM reasoning about which of the system's own bots or detectors is working, and why -- fed to opinion-arbiter as a trust discount, never a vote.

data_types.name: objection outcome
data_types.description: Whether a counter-argument's strongest objection was actually right, judged by brain-self-reflector from how the trade ended -- fed back to devils-advocate so its learned hit-rate per (objection kind, regime) can move.

data_types.name: online model score
data_types.description: A continuously-trained model's own prequential score for one of its slots (champion or challenger) -- each example judged by that slot's error on it before training on it, which is what makes the running mean a held-out measure without a separate validation split. Read by champion-challenger-gate in place of model-version.validation_score for a model with no discrete trained artefact for that ledger to hold.

data_types.name: broker token standing
data_types.description: Whether the day's broker session token is still valid right now, and until when -- the daily-expiry analogue of a venue's key-standing, since a broker session here is a whole login rather than a signed API key (spec section 3).

data_types.name: broker instrument listing
data_types.description: One contract as an Indian broker's own instrument master lists it: instrument key, exchange, segment, lot size, tick size, and -- for a derivative -- its expiry, strike and option type. Kept separate from symbol-universe because the shape genuinely differs (spec section 4).

data_types.name: broker market data
data_types.description: One trade or last-traded-price update from a broker's feed. Carries the same TradeFidelity distinction as market-data, extended with LAST_TRADED_PRICE_ONLY for a retail feed that states the exchange's last print rather than streaming every one (spec section 5).

data_types.name: broker candle
data_types.description: One OHLC bar from a broker's feed, same shape as candle -- kept separate rather than merged into it so this edit stays self-contained (docs/proposals/upstox-broker-adapter.md).

data_types.name: broker order book snapshot
data_types.description: Bid/ask depth from a broker's feed, same shape as order-book-snapshot -- kept separate for the same reason as broker-candle.

data_types.name: broker open interest
data_types.description: Open interest and today's traded volume/buy-sell quantity for one derivative contract, from a broker's feed. No crypto equivalent -- a spot/perpetual venue never published this (spec section 5).

data_types.name: broker option greeks
data_types.description: Delta, theta, gamma, vega, rho and implied volatility for one options contract, from a broker's feed. No crypto equivalent (spec section 5).

data_types.name: broker account funds
data_types.description: What a broker says is available right now, and how old that statement is -- span/exposure/adhoc margin, payin amount, notional cash and available margin, split by segment. Direct analogue of account-balance, kept as its own type because the field shape genuinely differs (SEBI margin categories, not free/used/total) and reusing account-balance would wire this into every existing crypto consumer of it via R-01 (spec section 6a).

data_types.name: broker price frame
data_types.description: Every tracked instrument's latest last-traded price on one broker, at one moment, published on a cadence rather than per tick. Direct analogue of symbol-price-frame -- kept as its own type because reusing that id would auto-wire this into every existing crypto consumer of it via R-01 (docs/proposals/broker-price-quote-samplers.md).

data_types.name: raw news item
data_types.description: One item exactly as its source delivered it: source id, url, title, body, published_at_ns as the source stamped it, observed_at_ns as this system first saw it. Both times, always -- replaying on publish time alone hands a backtest information the live bot did not have.

data_types.name: distinct news item
data_types.description: One story, with the same story from every other outlet collapsed into it. Carries the earliest publish time seen, which is the tradable one.

data_types.name: structured news item
data_types.description: One news item read into its schema-checked fields by the LLM foundation: what happened, to whom, the figures stated, the claim's tense.

data_types.name: news symbol tagging
data_types.description: Which instruments a news item names, resolved against the broker's own instrument listing rather than a hardcoded alias table.

data_types.name: news category tagging
data_types.description: What kind of news an item is: results, corporate action, regulatory, macro, halt, analyst, rumour or block deal. Routing depends on it.

data_types.name: news credibility rating
data_types.description: How far a source has earned trust, learned from whether its items were later confirmed by an official filing.

data_types.name: news novelty rating
data_types.description: Whether an item is new information or the same story rewritten and already priced. Distinct from deduplication, which removes exact copies.

data_types.name: news surprise reading
data_types.description: How far an outcome landed from what was scheduled or expected. A results print on its calendar date is not news; a beat is.

data_types.name: news item
data_types.description: The published news fact: the structured item, the instruments it names, the segments it belongs to, its category, its source's credibility. What every consumer outside the news block reads.

data_types.name: news impact forecast
data_types.description: For one item on one symbol: direction, how far price is expected to move, over what horizon, with what confidence. Learned from realised reaction.

data_types.name: news reaction label
data_types.description: What price actually did after a news item, per horizon. The training label the sentiment model plus the impact forecaster learn from.

data_types.name: news latency reading
data_types.description: Observed time minus published time for one item. Says whether this system is reacting to news or chasing it, and discounts a late item's forecast.

data_types.name: instrument restriction report
data_types.description: One source's statement that an instrument is restricted: F&O ban, ASM, GSM, circuit or halt, with the window it claims.

data_types.name: instrument restriction
data_types.description: Whether an instrument may be traded right now, merged from every source that reported one, each claim expiring on its own age bound. A level.

data_types.name: corporate action report
data_types.description: A corporate action as the exchange published it: split, bonus, dividend, rights or merger, with its ratio plus its ex and record dates.

data_types.name: corporate action
data_types.description: The price adjustment factor a corporate action implies, with the date it takes effect. Unapplied, a 1:1 bonus is a -50% candle every detector fires on.

data_types.name: market session state
data_types.description: Which trading session the market is in right now: open, closed, holiday, expiry day, special session. A level.

data_types.name: news source standing
data_types.description: Whether each news source is still delivering, when it last did, how stale it is. A dead feed reads exactly like a quiet news day unless measured.

data_types.name: news search request
data_types.description: A question asked of the open web: why did this symbol move when no known item explains it.

data_types.name: historical news window
data_types.description: Taped news over a replay window, each item carrying the time this system observed it so a replay cannot read tomorrow's paper today.

data_types.name: venue announcement
data_types.description: A listing, delisting, maintenance window or rule change a venue published.

features.name: K-line window builder
features.role: shape live market data into the fixed candlestick window the model expects

features.name: Kronos forecaster
features.role: run the Kronos model over a candlestick window to produce a price forecast

features.name: Kronos finetuner
features.role: adapt the Kronos tokenizer plus predictor to the assets actually traded here

features.name: Forecast scorer
features.role: score each past forecast against what the market actually did
features.note: Its scoring protocol is the neural-network best-practice list: walk-forward validation, time-based splits, no look-ahead, out-of-sample evaluation always net of transaction costs. docs/research/equations.md section 4.

features.name: Kronos size selector
features.role: choose which Kronos model size to run based on measured forecast accuracy

features.name: Implied volatility reader
features.role: read the option surface into implied volatilities at the strikes that matter
features.note: Switched off in spot and futures, which have no option surface. This is what R-02's switch is for: the part exists in every segment and only conducts where it can.

features.name: Volatility feature builder
features.role: compute the realised-volatility feature set from a candlestick window
features.note: RV 1d/5d/22d, downside semivariance over negative returns only, jump variance as max(RV-BV,0), vol-of-vol, ATM IV, 30-60 term slope, 25-delta put skew, market RV. All ten feature formulas, and the fact that features 7-9 need an options surface so spot and futures can only compute seven of them: docs/research/equations.md section 1.

features.name: Realised volatility regressor
features.role: estimate forward realised volatility from the feature set
features.note: The ten-beta linear model recovered from the reel's final frame. The ten-term regression written out: docs/research/equations.md section 1.

features.name: Regime classifier
features.role: classify the current regime with a Hurst proxy
features.note: Below 0.5 mean-reverting, above 0.5 trending, and mixed is a real answer. This is the detector the mean-reversion sheet needed but never named. The Hurst reading, its three bands, and why mixed is a real answer: docs/research/equations.md section 5.

features.name: Mean reversion detector
features.role: flag a symbol whose price has deviated far enough from its mean
features.note: Z-score entry above 2, exit below 0.5. Stands down when the regime classifier says trending. Z-score, thresholds, and the four conditions under which mean reversion fails: docs/research/equations.md section 2.

features.name: Volatility gap detector
features.role: flag a symbol where forecast volatility disagrees with the option market
features.note: The signal comparison E[RV10] against IV30: docs/research/equations.md section 1.

features.name: Semantic fact store
features.role: hold durable per-symbol facts under a closed-set key
features.note: Closed-set keys so a contradicting fact lands on the same key by construction and overwrites.

features.name: Episodic trade store
features.role: keep every closed trade as an immutable episode keyed on the condition observed
features.note: Append-only, written on close. Embed the condition, never the outcome.

features.name: Procedural playbook
features.role: hold the capped always-injected rule set that never gets searched
features.note: Never searched, so it never pollutes recall. A fixed cost every scan, which is why it is capped and holds behaviour rather than diagnosis.

features.name: Trade episode encoder
features.role: encode each closed trade keyed on the market condition that was observed
features.note: Key on what was seen, never on what happened. 'Lost 2% on a long' retrieves nothing ever again.

features.name: Lesson extractor
features.role: turn a trade episode into an instruction the hypothesis feature can work on

features.name: Expectancy decomposer
features.role: decompose expected value into separately measurable factors
features.note: The Drake pattern: a chain of separately estimable factors, so the weakest one is visible rather than the total merely being poor. The Drake decomposition it is built on, and the trade expectancy written out factor by factor: docs/research/equations.md section 6.

features.note: Built on CCXT.
