features.note: Built on CCXT.

features.name: Ablation harness
features.role: measure what breaks when each part is switched off
features.note: Proves R-02 and T-3 rather than asserting them. It measures only: the governor does the switching, because T-2 forbids a feature reaching into the control plane.

features.name: Source ingester
features.role: pull a source into text whatever form it arrived in
features.note: Books, papers, community chats, pages. The form is the ingester's problem, never the distiller's.

features.name: Skill distiller
features.role: distil a source document into a skill with its trigger described
features.note: Structure, not a summary: frameworks, decision rules, anti-patterns, per-section files. A summary is what makes an agent hallucinate confidently.

features.name: Skill index
features.role: hold every skill so one can be found by what it is for
features.note: Found by trigger rather than by title, the same reason episodes embed the condition rather than the outcome.

features.name: Skill loader
features.role: load only the section of a skill that the current question needs
features.note: THE mechanism. Procedural playbook rules are capped because they are always injected; a skill escapes that cap by being loaded only when relevant. The two are complementary, not competing.

features.name: Skill scorer
features.role: score whether a loaded skill changed the outcome
features.note: Lets a skill that never changes anything be retired instead of accumulating.

features.name: Leaderboard reader
features.role: read the public copy-trading leaderboards each venue publishes
features.note: Binance and Bybit publish these with official APIs. A front door, so no bot-detection evasion is needed or wanted.

features.name: On-chain position reader
features.role: read a tracked trader's on-chain positions from public explorers
features.note: Etherscan, Dune, DeBank, Arkham. Typed data that survives a redesign, unlike scraped HTML.

features.name: Strategy decoder
features.role: infer the strategy behind a tracked trader's position history
features.note: The 'decode' half of the user's words. Position history over time, not a single snapshot.

features.name: Edge comparator
features.role: compare a decoded strategy against what this bot already does
features.note: The 'or step up into us' half. Copying is the floor; the gap is where the value is.

features.name: Opinion arbiter
features.role: weigh the bots' opinions into one trade intent
features.note: Why the brain sits inside the segment bot. Three opinions in, one intent out. Opposing positions on one symbol are allowed while a bot is still in exploration, and after it graduates only when the regime reads mixed.

features.name: Profit lock
features.role: raise the stop as an open position gains so a pullback keeps some profit
features.note: Lives in risk, not in a bot, deliberately. It defends every open position whoever opened it -- if it sat inside the tailgater then a bull-opened trade would lose protection the moment that bot was switched off, and R-02 says every part can be switched off.

features.name: Bot scorekeeper
features.role: keep each bot's record of right calls against wrong ones
features.note: Pairs each opinion with what the trade actually did. This is what the bots learn from.

features.name: Feature reliability scorer
features.role: score which features preceded profitable trades rather than losing ones
features.note: The user's scorekeeping idea, moved out of the tailgater: it runs after trades close, not during them.

features.name: Edge graduation gate
features.role: graduate a bot out of exploration when its own numbers clear the bar
features.note: Bull and bear graduate separately, per segment, on measured edge rather than on a trade count or a date.

features.name: Cross-segment exposure watch
features.role: watch every segment at once to report total capital at risk
features.note: The one thing no per-segment block can do. Closes the hole the user accepted when choosing to split everything: risk allocation now sees the whole, while each segment still decides for itself.

features.name: Decision quality critic
features.role: score whether a decision was sound separately from whether it won
features.note: Learning loop scores outcomes. A system that cannot separate a lucky win from a correct call learns the wrong lesson with perfect discipline.

features.name: Regime break detector
features.role: detect when the market has changed enough that what was learned no longer applies
features.note: Distinct from the scanner's regime classifier, which labels the current regime. This one watches for the regime itself breaking -- the failure that kills systems that were working.

features.name: Open web reader
features.role: read the open web for ideas nobody pointed it at
features.note: Different from C-09, which decodes named traders, and from C-20's ingester, which distils a source it was handed. This one goes looking.

features.name: Idea generator
features.role: propose strategies nobody here has tried
features.note: Hypothesis is reactive by design -- it turns what happened into instructions. This is the generative counterpart.

features.name: LLM request router
features.role: route each llm-request to the cheapest route that still has allowance
features.note: Routing is a data-plane decision, not a control-plane one: this part emits a differently typed request, it never switches a caller on or off. That is what keeps T-2 and T-4 intact -- it names no caller, only data.

features.name: Subscription session caller
features.role: answer a subscription-routed request through the Claude subscription session
features.note: The user's Claude Pro/Max subscription used as the model backend, so reasoning costs allowance rather than per-token API money. Measured 2026-08-20 on this server: a headless call returned in 2.4s with the answer intact, so the mechanism is proven rather than assumed.

features.name: Metered API caller
features.role: answer a paid-routed request through a cloud model API key
features.note: The fallback the user chose for a spent subscription allowance: keep thinking on a paid cloud key rather than queue or go dark. Which providers hold those keys is not decided here, and no key is written into this repository -- see docs/secrets.md.

features.name: Subscription quota watch
features.role: report how much subscription allowance is left before the next reset
features.note: A bot running 24/7 shares one allowance with every interactive session on the same account. Without this part the router cannot know when to fall back, and the first symptom would be brains failing silently mid-session.

features.name: Paid spend ledger
features.role: record what the metered route spends against its ceiling
features.note: The fallback turns a fixed subscription into a variable bill. This is the part that makes that bill a measured number the router can act on, instead of a surprise at the end of a month.

features.name: LLM model picker
features.role: name which model answers a given class of request
features.note: The user's instruction for now: on the subscription account pick a model that is fast and costs little allowance. OPEN QUESTION the user left open deliberately -- once the whole bot is built, every model is to be experimented on. Because the choice lives in this one part, that experiment is a swap of this part, never an edit to a caller.

features.name: LLM response cache
features.role: return the stored answer for a repeated llm-request
features.note: One of the three reasons the user's own category summary gives for having a single LLM block: swap models, cap cost, cache. The cheapest call is the one never made, and on a shared subscription allowance that is the difference between a bot that thinks all day and one that stops at noon.

features.name: Unattended run warden
features.role: keep the whole system running with nobody watching
features.note: The user's first job for this block. Note what it does not do: it produces a restart-request, it does not restart anything. 'If part A needs part B running, that is the governor's problem, expressed through the control plane' -- transistor-rule.md, T-2. A warden that switched parts itself would be the second invisible graph that rule exists to prevent.

features.name: Venue outage rider
features.role: carry the bot through an exchange outage without human help
features.note: An outage is the specific unattended failure that loses money rather than merely stopping: positions stay open while the feed is dead. Separated from the warden because riding an outage is judgement about the market, while the warden's job is only that things are running.

features.name: Capability gap finder
features.role: find what the circuit cannot yet do
features.note: T-6 says grow by adding parts, never by making a part cleverer. Something has to notice which part is missing, or growth is whatever the last idea happened to be. Distinct from hypothesis, which turns closed trades into trading instructions, not into parts.

features.name: Part author
features.role: write a new part that fills a named gap
features.note: The user's second job: the bot builds its own new parts. It writes to the same part template every other part obeys -- role, consumes, produces, states -- because a self-authored part that could invent its own shape would end the uniformity T-1 exists for. What it produces is proposed, never live.

features.name: Part admission gate
features.role: admit a proposed part only after it passes every contract
features.note: The brake on the highest-blast-radius capability in this project. A bot that writes its own parts is a bot that can write its own defects, so nothing self-authored reaches the circuit except through here: the same check the pre-commit hook runs, applied to the machine's own output. Without this part, job two is self-corruption with good intentions.

features.name: Autonomy boundary
features.role: name which decisions the bot may take without a human
features.note: The user asked for a bot that decides without asking. That is a boundary, not an absence of one -- and a boundary that lives in one part is a boundary that can be read, changed and audited. Spread across nine parts as an assumption, it could only be discovered after it was crossed. It widens with earned maturity rather than by default. Reads the money mode since 2026-08-26: on paper the issued level is floored at act-within-limits, because competence is measured from closed trades and closed trades need trading -- a loop with no entry point that left 33 order intents refused against 444,545 zero risk limits. The level the evidence supports is still earned, and what may change settings or admit parts still follows it.

features.name: Trading halt decider
features.role: decide when the whole bot stops trading
features.note: Deciding without asking has to include deciding to stop, or autonomy is only ever a throttle stuck open. Risk allocation still owns the kill switch and still refuses for its own reasons; this asks it to be pulled, seeing the whole account at once as only a global block can.

features.name: Failing part detector
features.role: spot a part that has stopped behaving
features.note: The user's fourth job. The hard case is not the dead part, which is obvious -- it is the part still reporting healthy while its output has gone wrong. Rule 8 in the user's own standing rules says a display shows measured state, never asserted state; this is that rule turned on the parts themselves.

features.name: Part replacement planner
features.role: choose the replacement for a faulted part
features.note: Where self-healing meets self-building: the replacement for a faulted part is drawn from what the admission gate has already cleared. It plans; the governor swaps. A planner that performed the swap would be a feature switching a feature, which T-2 forbids however good its reason.

features.name: Survival tier monitor
features.role: grade how much runway the bot has left before it must conserve
features.note: Drawn from Conway-Research/automaton (src/survival/monitor.ts, low-compute.ts, read 2026-08-20). Its lesson is that scarcity is graded, never binary: high / normal / low_compute / critical / dead, each with different behaviour, and every transition recorded. Note what this is NOT: a part state. T-5 keeps states off/on, so the tier is data a part produces, which is also what lets any part read it without knowing who computed it.

features.name: Conservation planner
features.role: name what the bot sheds at each level of scarcity
features.note: The automaton's answer to running low is not to stop -- it downgrades to a cheaper model, slows its heartbeat, sheds non-essential tasks, and keeps living. It also holds a one-hour grace period at zero before declaring death, so funding has time to arrive. Both are anti-flap: a threshold crossed for a second is not a death. The plan is data; the governor still performs the shedding.

features.name: Autonomy policy engine
features.role: rule on each act the bot proposes to take by itself
features.note: From automaton src/agent/policy-engine.ts: every tool call passes one engine, rules sorted by priority, FIRST DENY WINS, and each decision is journalled with the rule ids and an args hash. It upgrades the autonomy boundary from a stated limit into an enforced one. Its sharpest idea is authority by trigger: an act the heartbeat started gets the LOWEST authority, below one the creator asked for -- exactly right for a bot that runs 24/7 unattended.

features.name: Self-modification journal
features.role: record every change the bot makes to itself
features.note: From automaton src/self-mod/audit-log.ts -- append-only, with the diff and a reversible flag, so the creator can see everything the agent changed about itself. The admission gate says what may enter the circuit; this says what actually did. Without it, self-building is unauditable, and an unauditable change is indistinguishable from a defect nobody noticed.

features.name: No-progress detector
features.role: spot the bot repeating itself without making progress
features.note: From automaton src/agent/loop-detector.ts: three identical calls is a loop and gets blocked; a repeated pattern of calls gets one warning then enforcement. It also keeps a list of idle-only tools -- checking a balance is not progress. This is the unattended failure that looks healthiest: every part reporting fine, the machine busy, nothing actually advancing. Rule 8 in the user's own rules, applied to activity rather than to status.

features.name: Upstream improvement watch
features.role: notice when a better version of the bot's own code exists
features.note: From automaton src/self-mod/upstream.ts, which fetches its own git origin, counts how many commits it is behind, and reads the per-commit diffs so the agent can decide whether to take them. Note where it sends them here: an upstream change is a PROPOSAL, so it goes to the same admission gate as anything the bot writes itself. Nothing enters the circuit unchecked because it came from outside.

features.name: Folded circuit view
features.role: compress the whole circuit into a view small enough to reason over
features.note: From WeaveMindAI/weft: any group of nodes folds into one node with a typed interface, so a 100-node system still looks like five boxes, and the AI builder searches the catalogue on demand rather than carrying it in context. This blueprint already has 66 parts and a part-health fan-out nobody can read. A part that must write a new part cannot first read the whole circuit -- so the circuit has to be foldable, or self-building is capped by context rather than by judgement.

features.name: Order flow state encoder
features.role: label each second of trade flow as one of fifteen states
features.note: From arXiv:2512.15720 (Mainak Singha, NASA Goddard). The state is the sign of the price change {-1,0,+1} crossed with the volume quintile {1..5}, giving fifteen. It reads trades, not candles, which is why this is a new part rather than a change to the kline window builder -- the volatility branch here is built on OHLCV and cannot see the tick sequence at all. Full specification, every equation and every threshold: docs/research/order-flow-entropy.md.

features.name: Flow entropy meter
features.role: measure how structured the recent order flow is
features.note: A 15x15 transition matrix estimated over a rolling 120-second window, its stationary distribution taken by eigendecomposition, entropy computed as the stationary-weighted average of row entropies and normalised by log 15. Rows with no observed transitions default to uniform. Separated from the encoder because the state definition and the entropy estimator are two things that will be replaced at different times. Full specification, every equation and every threshold: docs/research/order-flow-entropy.md.

features.name: Entropy magnitude forecaster
features.role: forecast how far price moves next from how structured the flow is
features.note: The third independent estimator of the same quantity, beside the realised-vol regressor and the implied surface -- which is what makes it a spare part rather than a rewrite. IT MUST NEVER PRODUCE A DIRECTIONAL OPINION. Entropy is invariant under swapping buy and sell labels, so it cannot carry direction: the paper measured 45.0% directional accuracy, indistinguishable from chance, and that is a theorem rather than a weak result. Direction stays with bull, bear and profit tailgating. Unproven here: 36 days on one equity ETF, VIX 14-22 throughout, 38.5% of the paper's profit from a single day. The ablation harness decides whether it earns its place. Full specification, every equation and every threshold: docs/research/order-flow-entropy.md.

features.name: Cointegration pair finder
features.role: find pairs of symbols whose spread has held together
features.note: From the statistical arbitrage reference sheet (p/DbPaMI1ndH2): Spread = A - beta*B, tested with ADF and KPSS, cointegration by Engle-Granger or Johansen. The equations existed in the research corpus with no part to live in, which is what this closes. Equations in docs/research/equations.md section 3.

features.name: Spread reversion detector
features.role: flag a cointegrated spread that has stretched far enough to snap back
features.note: The Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process dX = kappa(mu - X)dt + sigma dW says how hard the spread is pulled back, and half-life = ln(2)/kappa turns that into a holding period. That is the filter that decides tradeability here: a pair with a three-day half-life is real and useless to an intraday bot on 1m to 30m bars (RL-043). Separated from the pair finder because finding a relationship and timing its stretch are replaced at different times. Equations in docs/research/equations.md section 3.

features.name: Historical bar store
features.role: keep the recorded history a replay reads from
features.note: C-01 runs on live data by the user's decision (RL-024), which means nothing in the system currently keeps the past. A replay needs it, so this part is what makes backtesting possible at all rather than an assumption that history is lying around somewhere.

features.name: Walk-forward splitter
features.role: split history into training windows that never overlap the test window
features.note: The protocol both research sources independently insist on: the neural-network sheet gives walk-forward validation with time-based splits and never random ones, and arXiv:2512.15720 runs 10 days training against 5 days testing across five non-overlapping folds with thresholds frozen after training. A random split on a time series leaks the future into the past, and the backtest that results is a lie with a Sharpe ratio attached.

features.name: Execution cost model
features.role: charge each simulated fill what it would really have cost
features.note: The single most common way a backtest lies. The entropy paper's rule cleared 1,126 bps against a 1.57 bps round-trip cost calibrated to SPY's 0.7 bps spread -- on a crypto venue with a wider spread the same rule may clear nothing at all. Costs are a per-venue measurement here, never a constant carried over from an equity paper.

features.name: Instruction replayer
features.role: replay one opportunity instruction over recorded history
features.note: The engine. It takes what hypothesis wrote and runs it against the past, charging every fill. Five of the ten repositories the user was shown are backtesting frameworks -- vectorbt for sweeping thousands of parameter sets, NautilusTrader for an event-driven core built for correctness -- so this part has strong prior art and is a candidate for a dependency rather than a rewrite.

features.name: Look-ahead auditor
features.role: refuse a replay that used information it could not have had
features.note: A backtest cannot fail loudly. It returns a number either way, and a number from a leaking replay looks exactly like a number from a sound one -- which is why this is a part rather than a habit. It checks the three leaks that flatter a result: information from after the bar, windows that overlap between training and test, and a symbol universe chosen with hindsight.

features.name: Backtest scorer
features.role: score what a replay earned after costs
features.note: Reports per fold, never pooled only, and reports how concentrated the profit was across days. The entropy paper is the worked example of why: pooled it looks like +1,126 bps, and one single day carried 38.5% of it. A pooled number hides the thing that decides whether an edge is real or was one lucky afternoon.

features.name: Instruction promotion gate
features.role: let an instruction reach the scanner only after it has survived replay
features.note: This is what makes the block a gate rather than a report. The scanner is given proven-instruction, never a raw one, so an untested idea cannot reach live scanning by anyone forgetting to check. It is the same shape as the edge graduation gate that already governs bots -- earn the promotion, do not assume it. Reversible if the user would rather backtesting only advised: point the scanner back at opportunity-instruction.

opposing_positions.cost: Two legs means two sets of fees and, in futures, funding on both sides. In a chop both can lose. That is the price of the exploration phase and it is why the phase ends on evidence.
